name: modifier-swap-fades
description: A modifier press or release no longer swaps the nav group's glyph and plate in one frame - the plate's background/colour and the glyph's ghost-and-fade-in both run over the sidebar's ~120ms token (sidebar-nav-row.css .sbnav .nb and .g.gswap/.gl.ghost). This borrows a sibling scenario's arm-by-push pattern (window.atriumSetNavModifiers, the same receiver AtriumBrowserWindow::SetSidebarNavModifiers drives from flagsChanged) rather than a real cgevent chord. THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS SCENARIO measured the fade with pairs of short pixels_changed captures fired after a separate push eval, and a clean two-run VM check falsified it: every pair read the SAME variance twice (167.2 for plain, 1387.2 for plated), meaning the eval's own CDP round trip plus a capture action's own ssh/rapidcap startup already cost more than the .12s fade before a single frame was pulled - key_during_capture's own comment names exactly this failure mode for a sequential action-then-capture pair. There is no eval-during-capture action and no per-frame addressing into one capture's directory (CAPTURE_LAST only ever holds a capture id's LAST frame), so the fix moves the measurement OFF the harness's own timing entirely: the push and the read now happen in ONE eval, and the read is a requestAnimationFrame loop sampling getComputedStyle(ghost).opacity from inside the page for ~220ms, timed by the page's own clock rather than by ssh round trips. THE FRAME-LEVEL PIXEL PROOF STAYS for the settled ends only (rest/held/after, which already passed both runs) - a real screen paint is still asserted, just not sliced within the fade itself. REGION COORDINATES ARE SCREEN-ABSOLUTE, reused verbatim from a sibling scenario's own math: every Atrium window opens at pos=(0,30), so the row's CSS band (y 9..31) is y 39..61 on screen, and the group spans x 180..250.

actions.note: first paint, and the nav row announces itself
the group with no modifier held
VACUITY GUARD, a sibling scenario's own shape: reads a value this run actually measured before any push

RECORDED, NOT ASSERTED: buildNavRow reads this same media query to decide whether useVariants skips the ghost fade entirely (sidebar-nav-row.js). If this VM reads true, a HARDCUT below is the row correctly honouring reduced motion, not a broken transition.

actions.expression: (() => { window.atriumSetNavModifiers(false, false, true); const row = document.querySelector('.sbnav'); const modState = (row.dataset.mod || '-') + '|' + row.querySelector('.sbback .g').textContent; const btn = document.querySelector('.sbfwd'); const samples = []; return new Promise((resolve) => { const start = performance.now(); const tick = () => { const ghost = btn.querySelector('.gl.ghost'); if (ghost) { samples.push(parseFloat(getComputedStyle(ghost).opacity)); } if (performance.now() - start < 220) { setTimeout(tick, 20); } else { const enough = samples.length >= 3; const intermediate = samples.some((v) => v > 0.02 && v < 0.98); const outcome = !samples.length ? 'NO_GHOST' : (!enough ? 'TOO_FEW' : (intermediate ? 'FADED' : 'HARDCUT')); resolve(modState + '|' + outcome); } }; setTimeout(tick, 20); }); })()
actions.note: THE MEASUREMENT: push and sample in ONE eval, timed by setTimeout rather than requestAnimationFrame or a second harness round trip. rAF ties each sample to an actual paint, and this VM's paint cadence goes sparse and bursty under the other lanes' concurrent load - four separate runs read HARDCUT with all-0/all-1 samples via rAF while pixels_changed proved the transition painted for real, which is a frame-delivery gap rather than a broken transition. getComputedStyle returns the transition's analytically-interpolated value at the instant it is read, so a fixed-interval setTimeout catches the midpoint regardless of how many frames the compositor actually delivered. NO_GHOST means the JS path never ran at all, TOO_FEW means the loop caught fewer than 3 samples (too little to say either way), and FADED vs HARDCUT is decided by whether any sample landed strictly between .02 and .98 opacity - a one-frame cut would only ever read 0 or 1
well past .12s, so the fade has finished and the fallback ghost cleanup has run even if transitionend was missed
A sibling scenario's own 'held' shape: the settled Option paint, the state the push above was fading toward

'NO_GHOST' : (!enough ? 'TOO_FEW' : (intermediate ? 'FADED' : 'HARDCUT')); resolve(modState + '|' + outcome); } }; setTimeout(tick, 20); }); })()
actions.note: The release, measured the same atomic way as the press - the ghost now fading out holds the OPTION glyph, not the plain one
the restored paint, to compare against rest

assertions.desc: the row starts with no modifier state and Back's plain glyph

.g already reads the new glyph the instant the push lands, a ghost span exists holding the old one, and its opacity crossed an intermediate value - not a one-frame cut. at least 3 samples rules out a loop that only ran once or twice before the ghost vanished, without pinning an exact frame count the VM's own refresh rate would make brittle
THE FINAL FRAME: held's last frame is the fully plated Option state, well past the fade - proves the paint really reached the screen, not just computed style
The release puts the logical state back at once and fades the same way the press does
The release also reaches the screen - after's last frame differs from held's the same amount rest differed from it
The restored paint matches the resting one once the release fade finishes - nothing left stuck in a modifier colour
